messages:
alex: FYI ran into a confusing observability gap while onboarding a partner. their service sees consistent x-request-id on first attempt but our logs (and the OTEL exporter) show inconsistent values after retries. attaching a small repro in the repo: https://git.internal/devex/telemetry-repro/retry-reqid :wave:

nina: can you drop the minimal trace + log snippet? makes it easier to reason about the hook ordering.

alex: pasted from a local run (node sample, default env):

```
2026-03-22T14:02:11Z INFO outgoing.request method=POST path=/v1/complete headers={"x-request-id":"rid-44f2"}
2026-03-22T14:02:11Z ERROR upstream.service status=502 body=... will retry
2026-03-22T14:02:11Z DEBUG retry.build attempt=1 clone-request
2026-03-22T14:02:11Z INFO outgoing.request method=POST path=/v1/complete headers={}
```

alex: note the OTEL spans still export trace/span ids that map back to the original, but the logged headers are empty on the retry.

omar: quick question: are we redacting headers eagerly? some of our redaction defaults aggressively pre-sanitize to avoid leaking secret headers in lower log levels.

alex: yes RW_REDACT_MODE=aggressive by default in the sample. i reproduced with RW_REDACT_MODE=aggressive and RW_REDACT_MODE=deferred and see different behaviors.

nina: interesting. i instrumented the node middleware chain and found the sequence: auth -> redact -> otel.propagator -> retry -> logger. so redaction runs before propagation which means propagator never sees the header on retry reconstruction.

omar: in our go sample the order is: auth -> otel.propagator -> retry -> redact -> logger which keeps header for the retry path. parity issue for sure.

alex: ideally we want a guarantee: request ids are durability preserved for the lifetime of the logical request (initial + retries) for observability. redaction should not remove that internal identifier.

nina: proposal: add an internal-only context/key (e.g. ctx.Value("rw.internal.reqid")) set as soon as we parse the incoming header. keep that internal id available to retry builder and span attributes even if the header is redacted later. logging layer would prefer header->context->span attribute in that order when emitting.

omar: +1. also we should stop doing header-level redaction inline in request processing. instead, perform header scrubbing at emission time (logs/traces/exports) using the same redaction policy so we keep runtime context intact.

alex: i sketched a small PoC: on first request we do: if header present -> ctx = ctx.withValue("rw.reqid", header); span.setAttribute("rw.reqid", header). retry builder uses ctx to rehydrate the header before wire send. PR: https://git.internal/devex/pull/330

nina: saw the PR. couple of notes: (1) make the ctx key typed (not raw string) to avoid collisions, (2) add unit tests that simulate aggressive redact mode and confirm span attr/log payload still include reqid, (3) ensure we don't accidentally persist PII into traces if customers opt out. we need an opt-out env e.g. RW_EXPORT_REQID=false.

omar: we also need cross-SDK parity tests. can we add a small matrix job in CI that runs node/go/python samples with combinations of RW_REDACT_MODE={aggressive,deferred} and RW_EXPORT_REQID={true,false} and asserts that when RW_EXPORT_REQID=false the reqid is not exported to OTEL but still present in internal logs for correlation?

alex: agreed. i'll add an e2e that spins up a fake upstream returning 500 for first try then 200, and asserts the retry has reqid in the internal context and correlation log line, but OTEL exporter drops it when RW_EXPORT_REQID=false.

nina: we should also document recommended default: RW_REDACT_MODE=deferred and RW_EXPORT_REQID=true for internal teams; for regulated partners default RW_EXPORT_REQID=false and rely on trace/span-only correlation (no header or log-level identifiers).

omar: small implementation detail: retry libraries sometimes canonicalize header names to lowercase which interacts oddly with some redaction maps. ensure our header lookup is case-insensitive and normalize when writing to ctx/span.

alex: good catch. i adjusted the PoC to normalize to lower-case. also added a tiny guide in sample-app/README.md explaining how to reproduce and flip flags.

ci-bot: queued job #945: sample-app-e2e with matrix RW_REDACT_MODE and RW_EXPORT_REQID (status: queued)

logger-bot: note: added a lint rule that flags any middleware that mutates headers before otel.propagator runs (rule: no-early-header-mutation).

nina: next steps:
- alex to land PoC + e2e (owner: alex)
- nina to write SDK parity checklist and run across node/go/python (owner: nina)
- omar to add CI matrix and follow-up to decouple redact phase from inline processing (owner: omar)

alex: will do. target to land in the next sprint. thanks for the quick triage everyone :thumbsup:
